brief.text: File: app/(public)/auth/page.tsx (full content attached). Lines 57-61 currently render the OAuth sign-in error as a plain div with no ARIA role, showing {error} where error = error.message from supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth(...). Proposed change: add role="alert" and aria-live="assertive" to this div (or aria-live="polite" as a milder alternative) so screen readers announce a failed Google OAuth sign-in attempt. No other logic changes. Find the strongest reason this change is unsafe or wrong: consider raw third-party error string safety (XSS, info disclosure, phishing surface), whether role="alert" vs aria-live="polite" is right for this error, whether JSX text interpolation resolves any of that, and whether setError then setLoading(false) creates a race.

claude_position.text: Adding role="alert" (or aria-live="assertive") to the existing error div at app/(public)/auth/page.tsx:57-61 is safe and correct. It changes ARIA semantics only, no new data flow, no new rendering path, no auth logic touched. (1) XSS: {error} is interpolated as JSX text content, React auto-escapes text children, this is not dangerouslySetInnerHTML, so adding an ARIA role does not open any injection surface; the string was already rendered as plain text before this change. (2) Information disclosure: error.message comes from Supabase's signInWithOAuth client call, which at this stage (before token exchange, which happens in /auth/callback) is typically a small set of known error strings (network failure, provider not enabled, popup blocked, rate limit), not a stack trace or PII. The ARIA attributes only change whether assistive tech announces a string that was already visible to sighted users. (3) role="alert"/aria-live="assertive" is appropriate because this is a terminal failure of a user-initiated action that the user needs to know about immediately to retry, and it does not interrupt an in-flight OAuth flow because by the time this div renders the flow has already failed. (4) setError(error.message) and setLoading(false) are two setState calls in the same synchronous block after a single await; React batches them into one re-render, so no intermediate inconsistent state exists. Net: pure ARIA-attribute addition to already-escaped text content, no more risk than the existing unstyled div, closes a real accessibility gap.

codex_position.verbatim:
Strongest failure: this turns an untrusted third-party diagnostic into forced speech.

`error.message` crosses a Supabase/OAuth trust boundary without allowlisting or redaction. Making that raw string an assertive live alert can immediately vocalize email addresses, URLs, configuration details, OAuth state, or other sensitive diagnostics-potentially through speakers, screen-reader history, recordings, or shared assistive sessions. It also creates a phishing surface if any upstream/provider-controlled text can influence the message.

React escaping only prevents HTML/script execution; it does not prevent information disclosure or deceptive text from being announced.

Additional defects:

- role="alert" already implies an assertive live region; adding aria-live="assertive" is redundant.
- setError() followed by setLoading(false) is normally React-batched, so the claimed double-render/race risk is weak.
- The security flaw-rendering raw authentication diagnostics-is already present, but this change materially increases its exposure by forcing immediate announcement.
codex_position.gloss: Real critique: role=alert/aria-live=assertive doesn't create a new vuln class, but it converts a latent disclosure risk (whatever raw string Supabase returns) into forced, immediate, unavoidable announcement. Also correctly flags aria-live="assertive" as redundant next to role="alert", and correctly downgrades the race-condition angle as weak given React batching.

disagreement_matrix.claim: Announcing the raw error.message string via role="alert"/aria-live="assertive" is safe because React's text-interpolation escaping prevents any harmful effect.
disagreement_matrix.claude_view: Conceded. React escaping only prevents script/HTML injection; it says nothing about whether the plain-text content itself is safe to force-announce. error.message crosses a trust boundary (Supabase/OAuth provider) and could contain an echoed email address, an internal detail, or provider-controlled text, none of which was a problem when it was merely visible on screen but becomes a forced, immediate, unavoidable disclosure once read aloud or logged by assistive tech. Fix: stop rendering error.message directly; render a static, generic message ("Sign-in failed. Please try again.") on any error instead, so nothing from the third-party response is ever exposed through this element, on screen or via assistive tech.

codex_view.verbatim: error.message crosses a Supabase/OAuth trust boundary without allowlisting or redaction. Making that raw string an assertive live alert can immediately vocalize email addresses, URLs, configuration details, OAuth state, or other sensitive diagnostics-potentially through speakers, screen-reader history, recordings, or shared assistive sessions.

disagreement_matrix.claim: Pairing role="alert" with an explicit aria-live="assertive" attribute is necessary to get assertive announcement behaviour.
disagreement_matrix.claude_view: Conceded. role="alert" already implies an assertive live region per the ARIA spec; the explicit aria-live="assertive" attribute is redundant. Dropping it, using role="alert" alone.

codex_view.verbatim: role="alert" already implies an assertive live region; adding aria-live="assertive" is redundant.

disagreement_matrix.claim: setError(error.message) followed by setLoading(false) in the same handler risks a race or an inconsistent intermediate render.
disagreement_matrix.claude_view: Agree with Codex's downgrade. Both calls are synchronous state updates in the same event-handler tick after a single await, so React batches them into one re-render; there is no real race here. This was one of several angles I asked Codex to consider, and it correctly did not manufacture a finding here.

codex_view.verbatim: setError() followed by setLoading(false) is normally React-batched, so the claimed double-render/race risk is weak.

decision.chosen: Add role="alert" only (no aria-live attribute) to the OAuth error div in app/(public)/auth/page.tsx, and replace the rendered content from the raw error.message with a static, generic message ("Sign-in failed. Please try again.") so no third-party diagnostic text is ever exposed through this element.
decision.rationale: Row 1 is the decisive finding: forcing an assertive announcement of an unsanitized cross-trust-boundary string is a real disclosure/forced-speech risk, not a hypothetical one, so the fix must stop displaying error.message verbatim rather than just adding ARIA attributes on top of it. Row 2 is a smaller correctness fix (role="alert" alone is sufficient, aria-live="assertive" was redundant). Row 3 confirms no scope was cut short by skipping a real issue; the race-condition angle I raised in the brief was genuinely weak and Codex said so rather than padding the response.
